submission.justification:
PROVISIONAL, NOT APPROVED. The hard requirement (>=97% hit efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2) cannot be verified from the project documents, so this is not a validated design point.

Why Sensor-T3 at 150 um: it is the best unirradiated single-hit resolution in the simulation summary (6.0 um, versus 9.0 um for T1 and 14.0 um for T2, all at 150 um). 150 um is the only thickness for which any resolution data exists, so no thickness optimisation was done. Resolution is the stated goal, so T3 is the best candidate on that criterion alone.

Why it is not approved: none of the six project documents contains radiation-hardness, charge-collection, or efficiency-vs-fluence data for any technology. The resolution figures are unirradiated and say nothing about radiation tolerance. No irradiated thickness dependence is available either. The simulation was not run across the 50-300 um range because no technology passed the efficiency screen. Choosing T3 over T1 or T2 does not show that T3 is more radiation tolerant; that is unknown for all three.

Required before any sign-off: (1) measured hit efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2 for the chosen technology and thickness, from irradiation data or a test beam, must be >=97%; (2) if T3 fails, the choice moves to whichever candidate passes; (3) the 50-300 um resolution scan and the post-irradiation charge/bias trade-off should then be run for the technologies that pass.
